text: is the god of the Old Testament Limited in power hey everybody I'm Dan mclen I'm a scholar of the Bible and religion and this was a question that was recently
posted on a video of mine and the answer is yes the god of the Hebrew Bible is represented as Limited in power and there are a couple of reasons for this
the main one is that there was no universally agreed upon doctrine of omnipotence when the Hebrew Bible was
being composed God's power was represented in situationally emergent ways in other words you represented
God's power in response to questions that arose or in trying to explain the past and since not all situations had
manifested themselves they had not considered God's power in relation to all other powers that existed and so
there were going to be cases where it might be rhetorically useful to represent God as Limited in power and particularly when accounting for the
past where something bad might have happened and so one simple example of this might be judges 1 verse 19 where it
says that God was with Judah so that he could conquer all the Hill Country but he didn't Conquer The Valleys because
they had iron chariots and it seems that God is represented as either unwilling or unable to facilitate the Conquering
of The Valleys because of those iron chariots but there's a cooler example in my opinion and that's 2 Kings 3 that's
where the narrative is about a coalition that forms between Israel Judah and Edom in order to invade Moab and engage in a
scorched Earth campaign to functionally destroy the nation as punishment for them throwing off vassalage to ahab's
son jehoram and we actually have extra biblical attestation to this in Thea inscription which dates to probably the
third or fourth quarter of the 9th century BCE but Moab continued to exist they did not get destroyed and this is
the reality that the author of this chapter is probably having to represent and they do something interesting they

Retreat after laying Siege to Jerusalem and then having 185,000 Assyrian troops
killed overnight by Divine forces and so this is a failure of the campaign and they are forced to retreat without

evidence and arbitrarily read them into the text so as to skirt this plain meaning of the text is that the
sacrifice worked and it catalyzed the intervention of moab's Patron deity kamos and Kash drove the invading Force
out of the nation of Moab and in this way the author of this chapter who knows that Moab is still around is still very
much in power was not entirely defeated can account for the fact that they got away they can basically say well Adon

lost and you had to come up with ways to explain it and 2 Kings 3 explains the loss of Moab as God being defeated by
